For 45 British teenagers, it’s day one of Basic Army Training in Harrogate.
The Junior Soldiers of 19 Platoon continue their Army Phase 1 training at AFC in Harrogate.
Our raw recruits are now asked to confront the realities of soldiering, and the difficult truths associated with it, chief among them taking lives and risking their own.
In the four months of training so far the harsh physical and mental conditioning has taken its toll; there are only 40 recruits left now.
The 16 and 17 year old boys and girls of Army Foundation College, Harrogate are the youngest soldiers in Britain.
Allegations of bullying mean one Junior Soldier faces being kicked out for bad behaviour, while another tearful recruit wants to leave.
The discipline of army life has been a baptism of fire. But the regime is already transforming the teen recruits into young men and women.
To graduate from the Army Foundation College in Harrogate, Junior Soldiers need to be fit, disciplined and trained to kill.
The 16 and 17 year old soldiers of 7 Platoon survive outdoors for a fortnight of tactical exercises in the wilderness of Otterburn for their final stage of training.
The Junior Soldiers of 7 Platoon are now Privates in the British Army and dispersed across the length and breadth of the country to join their chosen regiments.

programmes.d: July 28, 1996. A bloated, decomposing corpse is hauled out of the English Channel. There is little to go on. Police don’t know whether this is a murder, a suicide, or just a tragic accident.
